newsitem.title: USA: Centennial Tech settles WebSecure suits.
newsitem.headline: Centennial Tech settles WebSecure suits.

text.p: Centennial Technologies Inc said Thursday it had reached an agreement in principle to settle claims related to class action lawsuits against WebSecure Inc.
Under the agreement, Centennial will be released from liability and will issue 345,000 Centennial shares and pay up to $50,000, for notice and administrative costs, to the class of plaintiffs.
Centennial said a number of issues remain to be negotiated regarding the settlement, and no binding commitment to the terms will become effective until a definitive settlement has been executed.
Centennial was named as a related party in shareholder suits against WebSecure, which was delisted from the Nasdaq SmallCap Market earlier this month.
The suits alleged, among other things, that WebSecure had omitted material facts concerning its relationship with Centennial in its initial public offering filing.

An agreement in principle to settle other class action suits against Centennial was announced by the company on Wednesday. The suits relate to alleged misstatements of the company's financial condition.

Under that settlement, Centennial said it would pay to the plaintiffs the proceeds of any recovery from its directors' and officers' liability insurance policies, and an additional $1.475 million in cash.
Plaintiffs would also get 37 percent of the company's common stock, which was delisted from the New York Stock Exchange in March.
Plaintiffs would retain their claims against former Centennial Chief Executive Emanuel Pinez and former Chief Financial Officer James Murphy.
